title: Review: Newton's law of gravitation and field strength; Coulomb's law; Gravitational potential and energy; Energy levels and spectra
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: F02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; C03-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game; C04-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; Q02-1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: C03-uk1#N.8, C04-uk1#N.10, F02-1#N.4, Q02-1#N.6a, C03-uk1#N.3, C04-uk1#N.1, F02-1#N.12b, Q02-1#N.13a, C03-uk1#N.9a, C04-uk1#N.6a, F02-1#N.8a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Resultant
items.clue: Single force found by adding each separate force as vectors.

items.label: Inverse-square law
items.clue: Pattern shared by gravity and charges: three times as far, one ninth the strength.

items.label: Gravitational field strength
items.clue: Quantity g outside a planet, varying as 1/r²: a quarter of its surface value at 2R.

items.label: Absorption line spectrum
items.clue: Dark gaps at fixed wavelengths, seen when white light has passed through a cooler gas.

questions.stem: Two electrons are held a short distance apart, far from all other objects. Which statement correctly describes the forces the electrons exert on each other?

options.text: They exert repulsive forces of both kinds, as their charges are alike.
Each electron repels the other electrically and attracts it gravitationally.
They exert only repulsive electric forces, having too little mass for gravity.
Their gravitational attraction exceeds their electric repulsion.

questions.stem: Point M is midway between two equal point masses. Point C is midway between equal and opposite point charges, +Q and −Q. Each pair is far from anything else. At which point is the potential zero?

options.text: At both M and C
At C only
At M only
At neither M nor C

questions.explanation: Potential is a scalar. At C, +Q and −Q give equal and opposite potentials, which sum to zero. At M two negative potentials add.

questions.stem: Two small charged spheres whose centres are 0.60 m apart exert electric forces of magnitude 1.0 N on each other. Their charges do not change. At what centre-to-centre separation would the forces have a magnitude of 9.0 N?
An atom has only four energy levels: −1.50 eV, −2.50 eV, −4.00 eV and −6.00 eV. What is the energy of the emitted photon that has the SHORTEST wavelength?
questions.explanation: Largest gap: −1.50 eV → −6.00 eV, ΔE = 4.50 eV. Largest ΔE → highest f → shortest λ.

questions.stem: Which statement is true for the gravitational field of a point mass but not for the electric field of a point charge?

options.text: The field strength is inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source.
The force on any test object placed in the field is always towards the source.
The field strength is defined as force per unit of a property of a small test object.
The field lines around the source are radial straight lines.

questions.explanation: Masses only attract, so the force always points to the source. An electric force on a test charge can point away from the source if the charges have the same sign.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which statement about the gravitational potential at a point outside a planet is correct?

options.text: It is the gravitational potential energy of any mass at the point, measured in joules.
It is the work done per unit mass to bring a small mass from infinity to the point, and is negative.
It is zero at the planet's surface and increases with height above it, as mgh does.
It is the gravitational force per unit mass on a small mass at the point, directed inwards.

questions.explanation: This is the definition. Potential is zero at infinity and negative at every finite distance, because the planet attracts the mass as it comes in. Unit: J kg⁻¹.

questions.stem: Two small charged spheres exert electric forces of magnitude F on each other. The charge on each sphere is halved, and the distance between them is reduced to one third of its value. What is the magnitude of the force now?
questions.explanation: Force ∝ (product of the charges)/r². Charges: ½ × ½ = ¼. Distance: 1/(⅓)² = 9. New force = 9F/4 ≈ 2.3F.

questions.stem: An atom has energy levels at −10.0 eV (the ground state), −5.0 eV and −3.0 eV. An atom in its ground state is struck by a photon of energy 3.0 eV. What happens?

options.text: The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to the −3.0 eV energy level.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 15.0 or 13.0 eV.
The photon is not absorbed, as it matches neither gap from the ground state, 5.0 or 7.0 eV.
The photon is absorbed, and the electron moves up to an energy of −7.0 eV.

questions.stem: Two equal masses are fixed a distance d apart. Separately, a charge +Q and a charge −Q are fixed a distance d apart. Which statement about the resultant field at the midpoint of each pair is correct?

options.text: It is zero for both pairs.
It is zero for the masses; for the charges it is not zero and points towards −Q.
It is not zero for the masses; for the charges it is zero.
It is zero for the masses; for the charges it is not zero and points towards +Q.

questions.explanation: Gravity only attracts, so the two pulls at the midpoint are equal and opposite. A positive test charge there is pushed away from +Q and pulled towards −Q: both towards −Q.

questions.stem: Two equipotential surfaces around the Earth are 1.00 × 10⁵ m apart along a radial line. The gravitational potential is −6.251 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ on the inner surface and −6.155 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹ on the outer surface. Taking r as increasing outwards from the Earth's centre, what is the average gravitational field strength g between the two surfaces?

options.text: +9.6 N kg⁻¹ (directed away from the Earth)
−9.81 N kg⁻¹ (directed towards the Earth's centre)
0 N kg⁻¹ (each surface is an equipotential)
−9.6 N kg⁻¹ (directed towards the Earth)

questions.explanation: ΔV = −6.155 × 10⁷ − (−6.251 × 10⁷) = +9.6 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, so g = −ΔV/Δr = −9.6 × 10⁵ ÷ 1.00 × 10⁵ = −9.6 N kg⁻¹. The minus sign means towards decreasing r: towards the Earth.

questions.stem: Three point charges are fixed on the x-axis: P (+4.0 nC) at x = 0, Q (+1.0 nC) at x = 0.10 m and R (+2.0 nC) at x = 0.30 m. Take 1/(4πε₀) = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². What is the magnitude of the resultant electric force on Q?
